A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conventional approach of CSI feedback may be sufficient for secrecy performance in some cases, but the unconventional approach of reverse training may be necessary in other cases.

in a system with a single transmit antenna and a single antenna for both the receiver and eavesdropper (single-input single-output system), the conventional approach of providing full CSI to the transmitter, the full CSI case, achieves a perfect secrecy rate of 0 b/channel use, whereas the reverse training approach achieves a perfect secrecy of 0.25 b/channel use at a transmit SNR of -5 dB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conventional approach is not always the best option for achieving secrecy.
the level of CSI should be carefully considered when designing a secrecy communication system.
, in order to achieve secrecy, it is necessary to avoid CSI leakage toward the receiver and/or the eavesdroppers.
